relationship: Moving an object relative to a converging lens changes where principal rays meet and therefore image position, size and orientation; moving a screen tests whether that image can be projected.

learnerLoop.action: Predict the image, move the object, and move the screen to test the ray construction.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Object distance determines real, virtual or focal-limit image geometry; screen distance changes ray separation at the screen.
learnerLoop.evidence: Principal rays, image markings and the screen projection show image type and whether the screen is sharply focused.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Explain the result and compare object positions beyond, at and inside the focal landmarks.

invariants: The ray construction, image position, magnification and orientation agree with the same thin-lens geometry.
A virtual image is shown by backward extensions and cannot be brought to focus on the real screen.
The focal-limit case remains distinct from a finite real or virtual image.
safeAdaptations: Adjust prompts, pacing and object examples while retaining object and screen manipulation.
Add comparison positions within the supported thin-lens model.
nonGoals: Do not replace the ray investigation with calculation-only exercises.
Do not imply that aberrations or thick-lens effects are simulated.
